rules: The Title Number and UPRN Look Up dataset covers registered properties in England and Wales associated with an address containing a UPRN.
HM Land Registry records addresses when property is registered and links them to Ordnance Survey AddressBase data where possible.
Where no suitable address exists, HM Land Registry can create a new address in its property gazetteer.
HM Land Registry later matches its created addresses and title numbers to new AddressBase addresses when they become available.
A title number and UPRN can be linked only where a relationship can be made between the AddressBase address and the title.
The lookup dataset is closely linked to the National Polygon and Title Descriptor datasets.
Title_No is a mandatory character field identifying the title registration.
UPRN is a mandatory integer field identifying a spatial address.
Address matching can produce duplicate gazetteer addresses when supplied information does not match the existing LRPG address.
An AddressBase address may have a UPRN but no associated title number when it is absent from the Land Registry Property Gazetteer.
The first national HMLR address database used Royal Mail PAF addresses, street-card indexes and local gazetteers.
In 2002 HMLR moved to LRPG using Ordnance Survey AddressPoint as the national address base.
In 2011 HMLR moved from AddressPoint to AddressLayer2 within Ordnance Survey MasterMap.
In 2014 HMLR moved from AddressLayer2 to AddressBase as its source of national addresses.
Postal addresses excluded from AddressBase have no UPRN and are not available in the lookup dataset.
Where a title affects many properties, all affecting UPRNs may be associated with that title.
If an AddressBase address has not been transferred into LRPG, the title can lack a UPRN even where one exists externally.
HMLR imports and matches an AddressBase change-only update approximately every six weeks.
Although associations can change several times during six weeks, published data shows only the latest change.
Access to the lookup dataset is chargeable and requires an agreed licence.
Updated files are available from the second working day of each month.
Customers receive the full dataset and validation files; the UPRN lookup product has no change-only file.
Delivery uses CSV with comma separators, double-quoted fields, UTF-8 encoding and a column-heading first row.
Full and validation filenames follow LR_UPRN_FULL_<MON>.csv and LR_UPRN_VALI_<MON>.csv patterns.
The entity search extension must be json, html or geojson.
The q parameter searches by postcode or Unique Property Reference Number.
The typology parameter accepts an array of typology values.
organisation_entity accepts one or more organisation entity identifiers.
The entity parameter accepts one or more entity numbers.
The curie parameter accepts one or more CURIE values.
The prefix parameter accepts one or more prefix values.
The reference parameter accepts one or more reference values.
The period parameter controls whether current or all entries are included.
A longitude point filter requires latitude to be provided.
A latitude point filter requires longitude to be provided.
The limit parameter controls the maximum number of returned results.
The offset parameter paginates the entity result set.
The field parameter restricts which fields are included in responses.
Explicit field selections take precedence over fields listed in exclude_field.
The quality parameter accepts one or more quality values for filtering.
The Environment Agency point-cloud archive contains highly accurate three-dimensional x, y and z points with component attributes.
Time-stamped DSM and DTM raster products are derived from the point cloud.
Point attributes can support bespoke products such as canopy-height or intensity rasters.
Site-specific surveys date from 1998, while archived point-cloud availability goes back to 2006.
Historic archiving means a matching point cloud is not guaranteed for every derived DSM or DTM.
Processing classifies returns into ground and surface-object categories.
Manual editing of the derived DTM means classified ground points need not match the final terrain raster.
Point-cloud data is delivered in 5km download ZIP files by survey year, containing LAZ files aligned to the OS grid.
Coverage metadata records survey start and end dates and attributes such as average point density.
The National LIDAR Programme divided England into 302 Phase 1 survey blocks.
Phase 1 blocks were captured mainly in winter between January 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat block surveys receive incrementing phase numbers rather than implying a complete rolling recapture.
National LIDAR products are published through the survey portal on an ongoing quarterly basis.
Products use 5km OS-grid tiles with filenames containing survey ID, grid reference and first and last survey dates.
National-programme LAZ point clouds classify ground and low, medium and high vegetation returns.
National-programme DSM products use the last or only return and include ground and surface objects.
National-programme DTM products use last-return points classified as ground and filter surface objects.
OS Terrain 50 contour vector tiles are supplied as one national MBTiles file in Web Mercator EPSG:3857.
Contour, spot-height and land-water-boundary attributes are mapped at zoom levels 9 through 14, not 0 through 8.
The GeoPackage contour supply is one national file with spot_height, land_water_boundary and contour_line layers.
